findings.passage: Mason, Christian, Richard and Christina were all killed by an AR-15 and yet today the first action we are taking in this senate body is to give a sales tax holiday so that people can buy more guns like this
findings.note: Floor remarks quoted by FOX 5 Atlanta during the Senate debate on SB 47, the gun, gun-safe and ammunition sales tax holiday bill, after the Apalachee High School shooting.

findings.passage: If we had the opportunity, we would have attempted to exclude those types of guns, no matter what you call them, that was used in the shooting at Apalachee High School,
findings.note: Floor remarks quoted by Georgia Public Broadcasting during the Senate debate on SB 47. He says an attempt would have been made to exclude the type of gun used at Apalachee from the tax holiday.

findings.passage: It's unfortunate that what we're doing today is extending from five to 11 days and giving an opportunity for folks to buy more guns like this. As I ask in my question, the gun that was used was legally bought, and so we are giving an opportunity for people to purchase these guns, whereas we could be trying to do something to ensure that we are keeping kids safe.
findings.note: Floor remarks quoted by Georgia Public Broadcasting on the SB 47 debate: he objects to lengthening the gun tax holiday and says the Senate could instead act to keep children safe.

findings.passage: And as a former educator who had a student bring a gun to school, having information shared between schools is critically important and can’t just stop at academics.
findings.note: Quoted by the Georgia Recorder (republished by Now Georgia) at a Senate caucus announcement of gun-safety bills. He supports a statewide system sharing student safety information between schools, citing a student who brought a gun to his school.
